did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 3 opens by describing a time when the word of the LORD was rare, and “visions were not widespread”—that is, prophetic visions were not a common occurrence in Israel.

Did you know? The text notes that “the lamp of God had not yet gone out” and that Samuel was lying in the sanctuary of the LORD, where the ark of God was. This places the revelation at night, near the holy site.
Did you know? When the LORD calls Samuel, his first response is “Here I am”—but he still thinks Eli has called him, so he runs to Eli.
Did you know? Only after the LORD calls Samuel a third time does Eli realize that the call is from the LORD. This reveals Eli’s role as a guide to the young Samuel.

Did you know? The LORD calls Samuel by name twice—“Samuel! Samuel!”—and Samuel replies, “Speak, for your servant is listening.” This describes his transition from waiting for the call to listening prophetically.

Did you know? The prophecy Samuel received concerned Eli’s family: his sons had sinned, and Eli knew about their actions but did not stop them. Therefore, the LORD announced that judgment on his family would be severe and that its guilt would not be atoned for by sacrifice or offering.
Did you know? Samuel was afraid to tell Eli about the vision, but Eli asked him not to hide anything. Samuel did indeed tell him everything, withholding nothing.
Did you know? After the revelation, Samuel grew, the LORD was with him, and not one of his words fell to the ground—a way of expressing that his prophecies came true and proved reliable.
Did you know? Samuel’s recognition as a prophet spread throughout all Israel, “from Dan to Beersheba”—an expression describing the land from north to south.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, it is emphasized that the LORD continued to appear at Shiloh and reveal himself to Samuel through the word of the LORD. In this way, Samuel became the central messenger of God’s word in Israel.
